oracle.why: Errata 37's independence is two implementations of one algorithm agreeing, which is what makes disagreement possible and therefore what gives a crosscheck its error-detecting power. Group F has one implementation. The TypeScript in reference/mochimo-wallet is the sole specification of this derivation; there is no C counterpart in reference/mochimo-core and no second implementation anywhere. These vectors record what the extension does. They cannot detect that the extension is wrong, and a Rust port agreeing with them proves only that the port matches -- which is the whole requirement here, but is a different claim from the one group C's crosscheck_typescript_expected supports.

vectors.note: A DigestRandomGenerator with no seed material. Both state and seed start as 64 zero bytes (:29-30) and both counters start at 1 (:23-24), so the first output is fully determined with nothing added. Pinned so that a port whose zero state or whose counter origin is wrong fails here rather than 2144 bytes later.

addSeedMaterial (:79) hashes seed || state rather than replacing the seed, so the order of the concatenation is observable. Two consecutive draws are recorded because the second depends on the state the first left behind.

vectors.falsifies: that the generator is a byte stream whose chunking is invisible to the caller
vectors.note: nextBytes (:86) runs ceil(length / 64) whole states and discards whatever the last one did not need, so two calls of 32 are not one call of 64: the second 32-byte call starts a fresh state and the first 32 bytes of the second state are never seen. Every field here is one run of a freshly seeded generator. A port that buffers the tail of a state and serves it to the next call is wrong, and passes any test that only ever draws 32 bytes once.

vectors.falsifies: that the seed cycles on every tenth call
vectors.note: stateCounter starts at 1 (:23) and is post-incremented (:70), so the `% CYCLE_COUNT == 0` test at :74 first passes when the counter entering the call was 9. The period is 10 and the phase is off by one from the obvious reading. The three recorded outputs bracket the boundary: call 9 is the last before the first cycle takes effect and call 10 is the first after it, so a port cycling on the tenth call differs at call_10_out while call_8_out and call_9_out still match. The call numbers were observed by wrapping the real private cycleSeed on a real instance; the byte fields need no instrumentation at all and are the stronger pin.

vectors.falsifies: that one integer-to-bytes convention holds across the derivation
vectors.note: Two conventions coexist on the live path and neither is a defect on its own. intToBytes (:3) writes four bytes big-endian and carries the account index into deriveSeed (derivation.ts:22). digestAddCounter (:35) writes four bytes little-endian into an eight-byte buffer and carries the PRNG state counter (:70). A port that picks one convention and applies it to both produces keys that look valid and are not. digestAddCounter is `private`, which TypeScript erases at runtime; these are the real method on a real instance.

SHA-512 over masterSeed || intToBytes(index), fed to a fresh DigestRandomGenerator as seed material, then 32 bytes drawn (:22-29). 255/256 and 65535+1 are here because they straddle the byte boundaries of the four-byte big-endian index, which is where a wrong-endianness port first diverges.

vectors.falsifies: that a negative account index is rejected wherever it is used
vectors.note: deriveSeed validates nothing. intToBytes(-1) is 0xffffffff by the shifts at :5-8, so a negative index derives a real secret and returns it. The value is recorded rather than the rejection, because there is no rejection. See F-validation-layer for where the check actually lives.

vectors.falsifies: that the derivation validates its index at one consistent layer
vectors.note: deriveWotsSeedAndAddress rejects a negative index (:34-36) and a tag that is not 20 bytes (:38), and then calls deriveSeed, which rejects neither. So the same argument is refused by the outer function and accepted by the inner one. A port that moves the check inward starts refusing inputs the extension accepts; a port that drops it starts accepting inputs the extension refuses. Both messages are recorded verbatim, including the double space the reference emits at :38.
vectors.derive_wots_short_tag_message: Invalid tag length, expected 20  bytes, got 19

vectors.falsifies: that "the address" denotes one thing in this package
vectors.note: Both calls start from the same master seed and both return something called an address. deriveWotsSeedAndAddress returns ww.getAddress() (:48), which is the 40-byte v3 address and begins with the 20-byte account tag. deriveAccount returns WOTS.generateRandomAddress(...) (MasterSeed.ts:123), which is the 2208-byte WOTS public address. Reading the code, both are "the address"; the two are not interchangeable and nothing in the type signatures says so. Note also that the 2208-byte address is generated under a 12-byte tag of 0x01 bytes hardcoded at MasterSeed.ts:123 -- NOT under the account tag -- so a port that passes the account tag there gets a different address for the same seed.

vectors.falsifies: that the derivation has only ever been exercised on seeds whose bytes are below 0x80
vectors.note: Every seed in every test in both upstream repositories is below 0x80, which leaves the high-bit path of any byte-to-text conversion unexercised. This vector drives the live path with a seed of 0x80..0x9f. The two call counters are the load-bearing part: both live entry points pass a random generator to WOTSWallet.create, which takes the branch at mochimo-wots/src/protocol/wallet.ts:243 and never reaches componentsGenerator. F-ascii-control is the control proving those counters can be non-zero.

The control for F-high-byte-seed's two zeros. Calling WOTSWallet.create without a random generator does reach componentsGenerator, so the counter is not stuck at zero and the mechanism measures what it claims to. componentsGenerator round-trips the seed through Buffer.from(bytes).toString('ascii') at wallet.ts:201, and that round trip is lossy above 0x7f in a way that is not a simple high-bit drop -- 0x80 becomes 0x00 and 0xff becomes 0x7f. Recorded as a property of the runtime named in this file's pin block; under the browser build the extension bundles the `buffer` polyfill instead of Node's, which is a second reason not to depend on this. It does not reach the extension either way: the only call site of the no-generator branch is createWOTSWallet at mochimo-wallet/src/crypto/kdf.ts:141, and kdf.ts is exported and dead. See invariants.rs::kdf_derivation_stays_unported.

The live restore path. createWalletAction (walletActions.ts:22-34) routes through fromPhrase whenever a mnemonic is present, and CreateWallet.tsx:60 always passes one -- so this, and not create(), produces the master seed a real wallet holds. fromPhrase keeps the first 32 bytes of BIP39 mnemonicToSeed (:55-56) and stores the mnemonic entropy separately (:52). The two are different values and only the first is the master seed.

vectors.falsifies: that a MasterSeed and the MasterSeed restored from its own phrase are equal
vectors.note: toPhrase with no stored entropy emits the seed AS entropy (:84-86); fromPhrase runs PBKDF2 over the mnemonic and keeps the first 32 bytes (:55-56). Those are different functions, so the round trip is not the identity: what comes back as the seed is not what went in, and what went in comes back as the entropy. This decides which value a port must treat as the master seed. The only caller that would persist the un-restorable side is SetupWallet.tsx:34, which passes no mnemonic -- and that component is rendered nowhere in the extension, so this is a hazard for a port rather than a live defect.

vectors.falsifies: that a port deriving wots index 0 correctly derives every other index correctly
vectors.note: One rotation of one account. deriveWotsSeedAndAddress calls deriveSeed on the ACCOUNT seed with the wots index (derivation.ts:39), so the index runs through the same four-byte big-endian intToBytes the account index does -- and 0 is the one value whose four bytes are the same under every convention. The indices straddle that field’s byte boundaries; the tag is held constant across the sweep, so a changed address is a changed index and nothing else.

The indices straddle that field’s byte boundaries; the tag is held constant across the sweep, so a changed address is a changed index and nothing else.

vectors.falsifies: that the passphrase argument is inert in the extension’s restore path
vectors.note: mnemonicToSeed salts PBKDF2 with "mnemonic" + passphrase (index.js:116,128), so a non-empty passphrase is a different 64-byte seed from the same words. MasterSeed.fromPhrase passes ONE argument (:55), so the live path is always the empty-passphrase branch and seed64_empty_passphrase is the value F-from-phrase’s master_seed is the first 32 bytes of. master_seed_first32 is the first 32 bytes of the TREZOR seed -- what the extension would keep if it ever passed a passphrase, and it does not. The two seeds are recorded side by side so a port cannot wire a passphrase through and still match anything here.
vectors.phrase: abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon art

vectors.falsifies: that the extension’s BIP39 usage covers every entropy width its library accepts
vectors.note: entropyToMnemonic and mnemonicToEntropy over a fixed synthetic entropy of this width: byte j is (0x10 * k + j) & 0xff for the k-th case, k counting 0..3 across widths 16, 20, 24 and 28. assertEntropy (index.js:34-36) accepts these four and 32; MasterSeed writes only 32, so nothing in the extension ever reaches them and a port that restores a 12-word phrase does. The checksum length is entropy.length/4 bits (index.js:51-57), which is why the word count moves with the width rather than with the phrase.
vectors.phrase: abandon amount liar amount expire adjust cage candy arch gather drum buyer

vectors.falsifies: that a mistyped word is caught somewhere other than the BIP39 checksum
vectors.note: The 12-word phrase of F-bip39-entropy-16 with its LAST word replaced by the wordlist entry one position later, modulo 2048. The last word carries the checksum bits (index.js:51-57), so this is the smallest edit that can invalidate a phrase. mnemonicToEntropy throws and validateMnemonic returns false by catching that same throw (index.js:107-115) -- so the two are one mechanism, not two, and a port that implements validateMnemonic separately has no second check behind it. The message is recorded verbatim because MasterSeed.fromPhrase never sees it: fromPhrase calls validateMnemonic (:46), which swallows the throw and returns false (index.js:111-113), then raises its own "Invalid seed phrase" at :48. This string is reachable only at the library boundary, which is where a user-facing port has to decide what to say.
vectors.phrase: abandon amount liar amount expire adjust cage candy arch gather drum buzz
